topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the lecture series and outlines the core learning objectives concerning cancer causes, carcinogenicity testing, and tumor initiation and promotion.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Intrinsic Risk, Genetics, and Environmental Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer develops through an interplay between intrinsic cellular errors, genetic predisposition, and environmental risk factors reflected in geographic epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Cancer Initiation, Metabolic Activation, and Tumor Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular and cellular mechanisms through which specific infectious, chemical, and physical agents cause DNA mutations or provide promotional inflammatory environments that drive cancer.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the analytical methodologies, including mutational signature sequencing, epidemiological biobanks, in vivo assays, and the Ames test, used to establish and evaluate carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion: Balancing Carcinogenic Risks and Practical Benefits
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer summarizes the lecture's core themes and closes the session with reflections on everyday risk-benefit decisions regarding environmental exposures.
